title: Honor D-Bus idle inhibits on the paths Chromium actually calls
head: 45cadff4564e
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: publishable draft with findings; not posted

leads.summary: Neither omarchy-settings PKGBUILD installs the new user unit
leads.consequence: The unit exists only in /usr/share/omarchy/default after packaging, not /usr/lib/systemd/user. On a fresh user, omarchy-dev/omarchy seeds the migration as already completed, then first-run's systemctl --user enable --now omarchy-idle-inhibit.service fails and set -e aborts the first-run unit setup. Existing users' migration can fall back to a user symlink, but that does not fix fresh users or the failing package fixture. Add install -Dm644 default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service "$pkgdir/usr/lib/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service" after the crash-watch install in both settings PKGBUILDs before packaging this PR.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3); corroboration, no change

leads.summary: If the shell starts before either runtime directory exists, its FileView never subscribes to later daemon state
leads.consequence: On a fresh runtime where $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy does not yet exist, Quickshell attempts to watch both the absent idle-inhibit directory and its absent parent. QFileSystemWatcher does not watch nonexistent paths, and nothing retries the watcher. When the daemon subsequently creates both directories and publishes an inhibitor, the initial probe (which printed a blank line) is never rerun: dbusInhibitorCount remains zero and the screensaver/lock still activate during playback until the shell restarts. Ensure the watchable directory exists before initializing FileView, watch an existing ancestor with a retry, or rearm a bounded probe on startup.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroboration, no change

leads.summary: Open PR #6572 adds the same daemon, unit and D-Bus name but writes an incompatible state path
leads.location: bin/omarchy-idle-inhibit:40-44; default/systemd/user/omarchy-idle-inhibit.service:15; PR #6572 diff bin/omarchy-idle-inhibit:STATE_FILE and shell/plugins/services/idle/Service.qml
leads.consequence: Both proposals add bin/omarchy-idle-inhibit, the same systemd unit and the same org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver owner. If both are merged without explicitly selecting and reconciling one implementation, they have an add/add merge conflict. A resolution that retains the #6572 daemon's $HOME/.local/state/omarchy/idle-inhibitors but this PR's QML (or vice versa) means the QML never sees inhibition; running both services concurrently cannot resolve the name conflict. Coordinate or supersede #6572 rather than merging the files independently.
leads.triage: factual; verified (#6572 open, same file names, different state path; intake/pr-6572.diff). Not published: the PR description already positions itself as the replacement for #6572; merge choice is the maintainers'.

leads.summary: Open PR #8955 replaces the same idleEnabled gate and has an exact-text test incompatible with this PR's uncombined gate
leads.consequence: #8955 changes idleEnabled to IdleModel.idleEnabledAfter(stayAwakeStateLoaded, stayAwake, mediaInhibiting), while this PR changes that exact expression to also check dbusInhibitorCount === 0. Taking either side of the merge conflict literally silently drops the other's inhibitor, and taking this PR's gate alone makes #8955's exact-text wiring assertion fail. A joint merge must compose both predicates and update both test expectations instead of choosing one gate.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (intake/pr-8955-view.json, intake/pr-8955.diff:123,282) and by Opus self-check (opus/upstream/pr-8955). Published as a smaller note.

leads.summary: Debug output reports dead-daemon state as active despite the live idle service treating it as zero
leads.consequence: If the daemon crashes with count > 0 and is not restarted, debug idle prints its persisted holders as active solely because the file is readable. The QML probe instead checks the PID and prints an empty line when it is gone. Thus the diagnostic used to investigate idle inhibition contradicts the actual idleEnabled gate on precisely the crash path; reuse the probe or validate liveness before reporting active holders.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N3); folded into the stale-state note

leads.summary: The supposed killed-client test actually has the caller exit normally before SIGKILL
leads.consequence: crash.py prints the cookie and exits immediately. The scenario sleeps 0.8 seconds before kill -9, so in the normal successful path the PID is already gone and this case only checks clean process disconnect, not kill while holding a bus name. To make crash reaping coverage meaningful, keep crash.py alive after flushing the cookie and kill it only once the state shows count 1.
leads.triage: factual; verified (test/shell.d/idle-inhibit-test.sh:73-86,160-163: crash.py exits before kill -9). Not published: disconnect reaping uses the same NameOwnerChanged path and the mutant for no-reaping is caught; low value.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at the D-Bus level the daemon does what the description says. It answers `Inhibit`/`UnInhibit` on `/org/freedesktop/ScreenSaver`, `/ScreenSaver` and `/org/freedesktop/PowerManagement/Inhibit`, drops a caller's cookies when it leaves the bus, and publishes an empty state on SIGTERM. The new tests fail when the Chromium path, `UnInhibit`, disconnect reaping or the PowerManagement object is reverted. The `idle toggle` change is needed and correct. Three issues look worth settling: PowerManagement inhibits also block the lock, the shell's state watcher can miss the daemon until the shell restarts, and the unit depends on a packaging change.

### PowerManagement inhibits block the screensaver and the automatic lock

Every PowerManagement `Inhibit` goes through the same `handle_inhibit` and `count` as ScreenSaver (`bin/omarchy-idle-inhibit`), and the shell folds `count` into `idleEnabled`. In Chromium 152, the two interfaces carry different wake-lock types (`power_save_blocker_linux.cc`, split since Chromium commit `50b7869d`):

```text
Chromium wake lock                       D-Bus name                        Counted
"Video Wake Lock" (playing video      -> org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver       yes
  on a visible page)
"Playing audio" (any recently audible -> org.freedesktop.PowerManagement   yes
  tab, including background tabs)
"Download in progress"                -> org.freedesktop.PowerManagement   yes
WebRTC active PeerConnections         -> org.freedesktop.PowerManagement   yes
```

In an isolated run on a private bus, a PowerManagement `Inhibit("chromium", "Playing audio")` produced `count: 1`, which the shell's parser turns into `idleEnabled = false`.

**Impact:** music playing in any Chromium tab or web app, a long download, or an open WebRTC call keeps the screensaver and the automatic lock from firing. This goes beyond restoring hypridle, which owned only `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver`, and the idle section of the manual describes it as "about locking and the screensaver, not power". The test "PowerManagement Inhibit persists" currently pins this behaviour.

**Suggested change:** do not count PowerManagement cookies toward the idle count. Either stop owning `org.freedesktop.PowerManagement` (Chromium skips a PowerManagement service with no owner), or keep answering it but leave it out of `count`, and change the test to assert that a PowerManagement hold does not disable idle. Chromium's video lock uses the ScreenSaver path, so video inhibits from Chromium are unaffected.

### The state watcher is armed once, on a directory that may not exist yet

`Service.qml` watches `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy/idle-inhibit` with a `FileView`. In Quickshell v0.3.1, `FileView` adds a watch for that path and its parent only when the path is set, and re-arms only on a path change or `reload()`. Qt's inotify watcher silently drops paths that do not exist. Nothing else in Omarchy creates `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy`; the daemon creates it on its first publish.

```text
idle service loads          -> watch $RT/omarchy/idle-inhibit  (missing, dropped)
                               watch $RT/omarchy               (missing, dropped)
daemon starts, publishes    -> creates $RT/omarchy/idle-inhibit/state
Chromium plays video        -> state count: 1
shell                       -> no event, dbusInhibitorCount stays 0, lock fires
```

This is based on Quickshell and Qt source plus a syscall-level replica of the watch setup: with `$RT/omarchy` missing, no events arrived even after an `Inhibit` made `count: 1`; with `$RT/omarchy` present, the watch picked up the new directory.

**Impact:** when the idle service loads before the daemon's first publish, D-Bus inhibits are ignored until the shell restarts, which is the original #6475 behaviour, while `omarchy debug idle` shows the inhibitor because it reads the file directly. From the install and migration scripts, this applies to the first session after a fresh install (first-run normally starts the unit after the shell is already up) and to migrations applied without a shell restart (the login notifier or a bare `omarchy-migrate`). On other logins nothing orders the shell against the daemon; which one usually wins was not measured.

**Suggested change:** create the directory before arming and then call `reload()`, as the stay-awake watcher in the same file does.

### The user unit needs the omarchy-settings install line

omarchy-settings does not yet install `omarchy-idle-inhibit.service` to `/usr/lib/systemd/user/`, and the PR's own `config-test.sh` fails on exactly that mapping. Fresh installs get all migrations pre-marked, so there only `enable-user-units.sh` enables the unit, and it passes all eight units to a single `systemctl --user enable --now`.

**Impact:** systemd checks every unit name before enabling any (checked with systemd 261 `systemctl --root`: one missing unit gives exit 1 and zero units enabled). Without the packaged unit, a fresh install would leave all eight units unenabled, including `omarchy-sleep-lock.service`, and first-run would retry at every login.

**Suggested change:** land this together with the omarchy-settings and omarchy-settings-dev install line. The open omacom/omarchy-pkgs#210 (written for #8452, same unit filename) already adds exactly that line to both recipes.

### Smaller notes

- **Optional test improvement:** the "dead pid" case writes `{"pid":1,...}` and relies on `kill -0 1` failing. That holds for a normal user but not as root or where pid 1 is the same user's process (as under bubblewrap). There the test fails, and because `fail` exits, every D-Bus scenario after it is skipped. Using the pid of a child that has already exited (for example `$(bash -c 'echo $$')`) keeps the intent; with that change the full file passed.
- If `org.freedesktop.PowerManagement` is already owned, the daemon exits and leaves `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` unowned too. This goes away if PowerManagement is no longer owned; otherwise the two names could be served independently.
- The pid check only helps when something re-runs the probe. If the daemon dies with holders and stays down (for example after hitting the restart limit), idle stays suppressed until the shell restarts. `omarchy debug idle` also prints those stale holders as active, since it does not apply the probe's pid check.
- Open #8955 changes the same `idleEnabled` expression and its test asserts that exact text, as this PR's test does for its own. If both land, the two gates need to be combined and both tests updated.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of all changed files, the idle service and the install, migration and first-run paths, plus Quickshell v0.3.1, Qt, systemd, Chromium 152, VLC, Firefox and hypridle source. Isolated runs (the daemon cases on private D-Bus buses) covered the daemon, the probe, the PR tests with mutation checks, the migration with a stubbed `systemctl`, and offline `systemctl --root` enable behaviour. Quickshell, a browser, a live session and a real systemd user manager were not run; the watcher issue rests on source and a syscall-level replica.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
